faqs.q: What does a bariatric psychologist do?
faqs.a: A bariatric psychologist helps people understand and modify their relationship with food through behavioral therapy and counseling. At the Bariatric Counseling Center, our clinical psychologist and licensed professional counselors work with clients on coping skills, mindful eating, goal setting, and family engagement as part of our comprehensive program addressing obesity, binge eating, and chronic overeating.

faqs.q: What kind of therapy helps with weight loss?
faqs.a: Behavioral therapy that addresses the psychological and emotional aspects of eating is most effective. We provide group and individual therapy, dietary guidance from registered dietitians, cooking classes with a professional chef, and mindful movement education in one intensive outpatient program. Our approach helps clients develop sustainable coping skills and a healthier relationship with food, whether as standalone treatment or alongside bariatric surgery or weight loss medications.

faqs.q: Why is it mentally hard to lose weight?
faqs.a: Weight struggles often involve emotional eating, stress, trauma, or long-standing patterns with food that go far beyond willpower. That is why we focus exclusively on the behavioral treatment of obesity. Our team helps clients work through the underlying issues, build coping skills, and create lasting change through counseling, nutrition education, and hands-on support in our teaching kitchen and movement classes.

faqs.q: How does bariatric surgery affect mental health?
faqs.a: Bariatric surgery can bring emotional challenges alongside physical changes. Our program supports people before or after surgery by addressing the behavioral and psychological aspects of weight management. We help clients navigate the mental health side of their experience through counseling, coping strategies, and ongoing support. For questions about surgery itself, your bariatric surgeon is the best resource.

## Frequently asked questions

**What causes stress eating?**

Stress eating happens when we use food to cope with difficult emotions like anxiety, loneliness, or overwhelm. It's a learned behavior, not a character flaw. At BCC, we help clients understand their relationship with food and build healthier coping skills through behavioral therapy, dietary guidance, and mindful eating education in our Intensive Outpatient Program.

**How do I stop compulsive stress eating?**

Stopping compulsive eating starts with understanding the emotions and situations that trigger it. Our program teaches practical coping skills, mindful eating practices, and personalized strategies to interrupt the cycle. We provide group and individual therapy, nutritional support, and cooking classes in one program, helping clients develop sustainable tools to manage stress without turning to food.

**What are ADHD eating habits?**

People with ADHD may experience impulsive eating, forgetting meals, binge eating, or difficulty recognizing hunger and fullness cues. At BCC, we work with clients who struggle with these patterns through behavioral therapy and dietary guidance. A licensed therapist or your medical provider is the right person to discuss ADHD diagnosis and treatment options.

If emotional or stress eating is affecting your life, we're here to help. Reach out to learn how our program can support you.

## What is nutrition counseling?

Nutrition counseling is one-on-one or group guidance from a registered dietitian to help you understand how food choices affect your health and weight. It typically includes meal planning, education about portion sizes and nutrient balance, and strategies for eating in different settings like restaurants or grocery stores. At the Bariatric Counseling Center in San Antonio, nutrition counseling is part of our Intensive Outpatient Program for obesity. Our registered dietitians provide nutritional and meal planning, lead grocery store tours, and teach you how to navigate dining out. We offer this guidance both onsite at our San Antonio facility and virtually throughout Texas, and sessions are in network with most health insurance plans.
